newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: RECORD DRUG HAUL CONFIRMED

The Customs Service has confirmed that a quantity of cannabis resin found on a fishing vessel off the New South Wales Central Coast on Sunday night is the biggest single drugs seizure made in Australia.
Customs spokesman Chris Schofield says the drugs weighed just over 11 tonnes, including the wrapping material, with an estimated street value of A$77 million.

Three men arrested at the scene have been charged with importing a commercial quantity of cannabis resin, and have been remanded in custody to appear in Sydney Central Local court on Monday. Investigations are continuing.
HOPES FADING FOR MISSING SAILOR
In the Southern Ocean, hopes are fading of finding British yachtsman Tony Bullimore alive.
An RAAF Orion aircraft has just turned back from the search area, after dropping a sonar buoy alongside Mr Bullimore's capsized yacht.
The buoy is designed to pick up any sounds from the hull of the yacht, where it's believed the Englishman may be taking refuge, and defence officials are now waiting for reports from the Orion crew.
The guided missile frigate, HMAS Adelaide, is on its way to the area to launch a search helicopter, but poor weather is delaying its progress.
Defence spokesman, Colonel Andrew Reynolds, says there's been no reactivation of Mr Bullimore's rescue beacon.
PORT HEDLAND LUCKY TO ESCAPE DAMAGE
In Western Australia, the State Emergency Service says the north west town of Port Hedland was extremely lucky to escape serious damage from tropical cyclone Rachel.
The town suffered only superficial damage, mainly to rooves, fencing and vegetation. Regional manager for the SES, Dennis Rayner, says Port Hedland residents are relieved.
PLANE CRASH IN NORTH QUEENSLAND KILLS ONE

A plane has crashed in North Queensland, killing the pilot. Police say the plane's crashed at Bloomsbury, about 100 kilometres north of Mackay. It's believed the pilot of the light plane was the only occupant.
VIETNAMESE COUPLE BASHED AT SURFERS

A Vietnamese-born couple has returned home to Sydney, after being kicked and beaten in front of their children, busloads of tourists and motorists outside a Surfers Paradise service station. The attack occurred on Monday night.
Police say Loi Dao and his wife, Huong Phang, both 35, required medical attention after the incident.
They say a woman swore at Mr Doa and told him to go home.
He retorted and the woman's male companion rushed at him and punched him. Mr Dao's wife ran to his aid but the woman kicked her in the abdomen.
ACB CHIEF GIVES FULL SUPPORT TO TAYLOR

Chief Executive of the Australian Cricket Board Graham Halbisch says Australian captain Mark Taylor may need to get more selfish about his game, in a bid to lift himself out of a form slump. Mr Halbisch has given his full support to Taylor.
In his last 22 first-class innings, Taylor has scored only one half century, and in his six one-day internationals this summer has a top score of only 29.
Halbisch says perhaps Taylor should temporarily forget about the rest of the side and worry about his own game.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
